ev.q: Coverage among Asian persons was higher than that among persons of other races and ethnicities
Data collected during July 1–September 30, 2022, indicate that overall, 47.2% of children and adolescents received ≥1 COVID-19 vaccine dose
Kaplan-Meier estimation methods were used to calculate cumulative ≥1-dose COVID-19 vaccination coverage
By August 31, 2022, 33.2%, 59.0%, and 68.6% of persons aged 5–11, 12–15, and 16–17 years, respectively, had received ≥1 COVID-19 vaccine dose
Coverage in Black children aged 5–11 years was 4.0 to 33.6 percentage points lower than that among Asian, Hispanic, and other/multiple race children
Coverage among Asian and Hispanic children and adolescents was higher in most sociodemographic subgroups compared with coverage among White children and adolescents.
CDC analyzed data from the National Immunization Survey–Child COVID Module (NIS-CCM)
NIS-CCM is a nationally representative random-digit–dialed mobile telephone survey of households

methods_quotes.q: Kaplan-Meier estimation methods were used to calculate cumulative ≥1-dose COVID-19 vaccination coverage as of August 31, 2022.
Differences in ≥1-dose coverage were assessed by race and ethnicity and stratified by sociodemographic subgroups.
Pairwise comparisons were conducted to assess differences in ≥1-dose estimates for all races and ethnicities.
Survey weights were used to adjust to the noninstitutionalized U.S. population of children and adolescents
Cumulative percentage vaccinated with ≥1 dose was estimated using Kaplan Meier survival analysis techniques
Estimates were suppressed because they did not meet standards for data reliability (CI >20, relative SE >30, or sample size <30).
